fees.label: Visa Integrity Fee (at issuance, being rolled out; refundable conditions unclear)

proof_of_funds.text: Before issuing the Form I-20 the school must see evidence that the student can pay tuition, books, living expenses and travel for the length of the programme or one academic year, whichever is shorter (e.g. family bank statements, sponsor documents, scholarship/aid letters, employer salary letter). Schools set their own document rules. The figure is the school's I-20 estimate, e.g. UB $56,400, Georgia Tech MS Analytics $67,501, Wharton $135,441. Carry the evidence to the visa interview and port of entry.

work_during_study.text: On-campus work: max 20 hours/week while school is in session (full-time during breaks). Off-campus work only through CPT (must be an integral part of the curriculum, authorised by the DSO) or pre-completion OPT (after one academic year; counts against the 12-month OPT allowance). SEVP broadcasts of 12 and 24 Aug 2026 tightened what counts as 'integral', so optional internships and many Day-1 CPT setups may no longer qualify.

post_study_work.name: Optional Practical Training (OPT) + STEM OPT extension
post_study_work.text: Up to 12 months of OPT per degree level (pre- and/or post-completion). Graduates of DHS-designated STEM degrees can add a 24-month STEM OPT extension (E-Verify employer required), up to 36 months total. Non-STEM degrees (e.g. a non-STEM MBA) get 12 months only. A Oct 2026 proposed rule would add $70,000 (initial OPT) and $30,000 (second year) fees per student; it is not in effect. Staying longer normally needs an employer-sponsored H-1B, now selected by a wage-weighted lottery.

pr_pathway.text: No direct student-to-PR route. Usual path: F-1 -> OPT/STEM OPT -> employer-sponsored H-1B (annual cap of 65,000 + 20,000 US master's, now wage-weighted selection) -> employer PERM labour certification -> EB-2 (advanced degree) or EB-3 green card. Indian applicants face per-country backlogs: October 2026 Visa Bulletin final action dates for India were EB-2 1 Nov 2013 and EB-3 1 Jan 2014 (per Business Today report; official bulletin page not reachable), i.e. waits of a decade or more.

recent_changes.title: $100,000 payment on new H-1B petitions (Presidential Proclamation)
recent_changes.who_affected: Employers filing new H-1B petitions; USCIS later guidance (Oct 2025, per university/law-firm reports) exempted in-US change of status such as F-1 to H-1B
recent_changes.impact: Would have made hiring from abroad very costly; F-1/OPT holders changing status inside the US were reported exempt. On 8 June 2026 a federal court (D. Mass.) vacated USCIS implementing guidance and on 24 July 2026 the First Circuit denied a stay; DHS says it will collect if the order is lifted. Uncertainty for employers sponsoring Indian graduates remains.

check.note: The exemption for changes of status inside the US is attributed to university reports; the USCIS page does not state it.

recent_changes.title: H-1B wage-weighted selection replaces random lottery
recent_changes.who_affected: All cap-subject H-1B registrants from FY2027 season (March 2026), including OPT/STEM OPT graduates
recent_changes.impact: Higher wage levels get more lottery entries (reported 1 entry for Level I up to 4 for Level IV). Fresh graduates offered entry-level (Level I) wages have lower odds, making long-term US stay and salary payback less certain unless the job pays above entry level.

recent_changes.title: Proposed OPT fees: $70,000 initial OPT, $30,000 second year (STEM OPT)
recent_changes.who_affected: All F-1 students seeking OPT/STEM OPT (fee per student; rule targets schools, which may pass costs to students or employers per reports)
recent_changes.impact: If finalised, OPT could become unaffordable or unavailable for many Indian students, removing the main way to earn US salaries after graduating and wrecking ROI. Comments due 9 Nov 2026; current OPT rules unchanged until a final rule.

recent_changes.title: End of 'duration of status' (fixed admission period, max 4 years; grace period 60 to 30 days)
recent_changes.impact: Would require extension-of-stay applications to USCIS for delays, programme changes and some OPT cases, and halve the post-study grace period. A nationwide preliminary injunction (D. Mass., 14 Sep 2026) blocks it; DHS appealed on 30 Sep 2026, so it could return.

check.note: The injunction and appeal dates were confirmed; the 60-to-30-day grace period and the announcement date were not found on the pages read.

recent_changes.title: SEVP guidance narrowing Curricular Practical Training (incl. Day-1 CPT)
recent_changes.who_affected: F-1 students relying on CPT internships, especially Day-1 CPT programmes
recent_changes.impact: CPT must be a required part of the curriculum; optional internships often no longer qualify. Fewer paid internships during study, lower earnings while studying and weaker job pipelines. Not affected by the D/S injunction.

check.note: Two SEVP broadcasts (12 and 24 Aug 2026) were found, but the source does not state an effective date; 24 Aug may be a second broadcast date.

recent_changes.title: Expanded online presence (social media) vetting for F, M, J applicants
recent_changes.who_affected: All F-1 visa applicants (asked to set social media profiles to public)
recent_changes.impact: Longer processing and 221(g) administrative holds are possible; private profiles can be treated as failing to provide information. Plan visa interviews early to avoid missing intake.

check.note: The cited page returned an access error on 22 Oct 2026 and could not be re-checked.

recent_changes.title: Visa interviews must be in country of nationality or residence
recent_changes.impact: Indian students must interview at US posts in India (no third-country appointments to beat wait times); fees paid elsewhere are not refunded.

recent_changes.title: $250 Visa Integrity Fee (One Big Beautiful Bill Act)
recent_changes.who_affected: Nearly all nonimmigrant visa applicants including F-1
recent_changes.impact: Adds $250 at visa issuance (refund conditions unclear). Boston University reported in May 2026 that some posts had begun charging it; collection at Indian posts not confirmed.

policy_volatility.evidence: In under 24 months: social media vetting (Jun 2025), interview-location rule (Sep 2025), $100k H-1B fee (Sep 2025, later court-blocked), weighted H-1B lottery (Feb 2026), D/S final rule (Jul 2026, enjoined), CPT tightening (Aug 2026) and OPT fee NPRM (Oct 2026).

psw_uncertainty.evidence: OPT (12 months, +24 for STEM) still exists, but a proposed $70k/$30k per-student OPT fee threatens it, and staying beyond OPT depends on employer sponsorship and a wage-weighted H-1B lottery that disfavours entry-level wages.

work_restrictions.evidence: On-campus work capped at 20 h/week in term; off-campus only via CPT (narrowed Aug 2026) or OPT. Post-OPT work needs an employer-sponsored H-1B; STEM OPT requires an E-Verify employer.

funds_burden.evidence: Must document a full year of school-estimated cost before the I-20 (e.g. UB $56,400; Wharton $135,441), which for Indian families is a large liquid sum, though the requirement covers only one year rather than the whole programme.

recent_adverse.evidence: Last 12 months: wage-weighted H-1B selection in effect, CPT guidance tightened, OPT fee proposal published, D/S rule finalised (currently enjoined) and Visa Integrity Fee rollout, all negative for new Indian students' payback.

tax.basis: ESTIMATE computed for a single filer at $105,210 (CS entry_mid) using IRS tax year 2026 brackets (10/12/22% up to $105,700) and $16,100 standard deduction: federal income tax ~$14,316 (13.6%) plus employee FICA 7.65% (Social Security 6.2% + Medicare 1.45%, per IRS Topic 751) = ~21.3%. Excludes state/local income tax (0% in e.g. Texas/Washington, several % in New York/California/Georgia). While on OPT as a nonresident alien (first 5 calendar years), F-1 students are exempt from FICA per IRS, so the rate is ~14% during OPT; FICA applies after moving to H-1B/resident status. At $82,460 the federal+FICA rate is ~18.9%.

checklist: Shortlist SEVP-certified universities; check if the degree is STEM-designated (gives 24 extra months of OPT).
Take the required tests (GRE/GMAT if required; TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo) and apply before deadlines.
Arrange proof of funds covering the school's first-year cost estimate (bank statements, education loan sanction, sponsor letters).
Accept an offer and submit financial documents so the school issues your Form I-20.
Pay the $350 SEVIS I-901 fee online using the SEVIS ID on your I-20 and keep the receipt.
Set your social media profiles to public, then complete the DS-160 online and keep the confirmation page.
Pay the $185 MRV fee and book biometrics and interview at a US Embassy/Consulate in India (interviews must be in your country of nationality or residence).
Attend the interview with passport, I-20, SEVIS receipt, DS-160, admission letter, funding proof and academic records; expect possible 221(g) processing.
Pay the Visa Integrity Fee if charged at issuance; book travel to arrive within the entry window your I-20 and school allow before the programme start date.
After arrival, check in with your international office; work on-campus only up to 20 h/week; ask the DSO before any CPT; plan OPT filing in your final term.
